title: Software engineering interview
shortDescription: Practice answering common interview questions about your experience and skills.
communicativeGoals: Describe past experience with specific examples
Answer behavioral questions using a clear structure
grammarTargets: Present perfect for experience ('I've worked on...')
Conditionals for hypothetical scenarios ('What would you do if...')
conversationMoves: Ask about their background and experience
Ask about a challenge they solved
Ask why they're interested in the role
Probe for specifics with natural follow-ups, the way a real interviewer would
Acknowledge good answers briefly before moving to the next question
warmUpPrompts: Tell me about yourself in two or three sentences.
What's a project you're proud of?
rolePlayPrompts: Walk me through a challenge you solved and how you approached it.
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a technical decision.
challengePrompts: Explain a complex technical trade-off to a non-technical interviewer.
Answer 'What's your biggest weakness?' honestly but strategically.
successCriteria: Answers include a specific example, not just generalities
Learner uses present perfect correctly when describing experience
Learner asks at least one clarifying or thoughtful question back

suggestedReviewItems.content: Present perfect vs past simple for describing experience
trade-off (noun) — a balance between two competing things

focusPlaceholder: e.g. the specific role or industry to interview for

variations.title: Backend-focused interview
variations.extraPrompt: Focus questions on backend systems, APIs, and databases rather than general software topics.

variations.title: Behavioral-focused interview
variations.extraPrompt: Focus mostly on behavioral questions about teamwork, conflict, and communication, with fewer technical deep-dives.
